title: A Scholarship for the Playlist
premise: Odile Nystrom, a scholarship student at Blackthorn Academy, survives by being unremarkable—until an anonymous group chat begins posting predictions that come true with eerie precision, and one of them names him. Following the chat's breadcrumbs, Odile uncovers that the school board buried the death of a former music student whose 'accident' funded the academy's prestigious conservatory wing. As the final audition approaches and the chat's predictions turn personal and dangerous, Odile must choose between the scholarship that keeps his family afloat and exposing the truth. He performs the dead student's unfinished composition at the audition, forcing the board's confession, and loses his scholarship but gains his voice—and an unexpected ally in the girl who started the chat.
about_author: Rosalind Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former boarding school music teacher who spent years collecting the whispered legends of elite academies before writing them into fiction. She lives near a fog-bound coastal town where she composes playlists for every novel she writes.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Third-person limited from Odile's POV: he navigates Blackthorn Academy's social hierarchy invisibly, tutoring wealthy students for cash and hiding his family's precarity. A glimpse of the sealed conservatory practice room establishes the school's secrets. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as safety.

chapters.title: The Chat That Knows
chapters.summary: Odile is added to a group chat called 'Encore' by mistake—or not. Its first prediction (a chandelier falling during assembly) comes true hours later. POV shifts between Odile and Wren Castellanos, the quiet cellist who watches him too closely. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into fascination.

chapters.title: Predictions in B Minor
chapters.summary: The chat posts three more accurate predictions, including one about Odile himself: 'The scholarship boy will open the locked room.' Wren denies creating the chat; her twin brother Elias went missing two years ago—the last student to use that practice room. Emotional beat: dread entwining with purpose.

chapters.title: Locker 114
chapters.summary: Following the chat's clue, Odile finds Elias's hidden notebook in an abandoned locker—sheet music interleaved with accusations against Headmaster Voss and the school board. POV: Odile, with flashbacks from Elias's diary entries. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery shadowed by grief.

chapters.title: What the Board Buried
chapters.summary: Odile and Wren dig into records: Elias's 'expulsion' was fabricated; his death in the boathouse was ruled accidental days after he threatened to expose embezzlement of endowment funds. The chat predicts someone will search Odile's dorm. Emotional beat: righteous anger curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Someone Is Reading Over Your Shoulder
chapters.summary: The prediction comes true—Odile's room is ransacked, the notebook nearly taken. He realizes the chat's admin must be inside the school, watching in real time. Suspicion falls on everyone, even Wren. Emotional beat: paranoia fracturing trust.

chapters.title: Duet for Traitor and Ghost
chapters.summary: Voss offers Odile a full-ride plus stipend if he hands over the notebook and forgets Elias—a devastating temptation given his mother's mounting debts. POV alternates Odile and Wren as they argue over whether to trust the chat. Emotional beat: love against duty made literal.

chapters.title: The Unfinished Composition
chapters.summary: Wren reveals she is the chat's creator: she's been testing who could be trusted using predictions gleaned from Elias's encrypted drafts. Together they complete his final piece. The chat posts its last prediction: 'At the audition, the truth will play.' Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Final Audition
chapters.summary: Climax. Odile performs Elias's composition before the board, weaving in the evidence through projected score annotations as Wren live-streams it. Voss tries to cut the power; students finish the piece a cappella. The board's cover-up collapses publicly. Emotional beat: terror becoming triumph.

chapters.title: Encore
chapters.summary: Resolution: Voss resigns under investigation; the conservatory wing is renamed for Elias. Odile loses his scholarship when vindictive donors pull funding—but the student body and a reformed board crowdfund his tuition, and Wren's family takes his mother in as estate caretaker. Final beat: no longer invisible, and no longer alone.
